clue.text: Shake fist at first, then rewrite paper

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word fist is taken
to rewrite something is to set its letters down again in a new order

explanation.surface: An angry writer brandishes a fist before tearing up a draft and starting the paper over.
explanation.walkthrough: A frappe is the New England name for a milkshake, so 'Shake' is a noun here, not the angry gesture it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of the US, especially New England, a thick blended milk drink is called a frappe.

clue.text: Ali's extremities, making a weak foundation

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay, so his feet belonged to Clay
second meaning: a hidden flaw that undermines something seemingly strong

explanation.walkthrough: The boxer Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical idiom, from Daniel's statue standing on clay feet, names a hidden weakness in something admired.

clue.text: She didn't want to lose the thread of a song with reversed coda

definitions.text: She didn't want to lose the thread

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: the word for coda is written backwards

parts.note: a coda is the end of a piece

explanation.surface: A singer worried about losing track in a song whose closing section has been flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth she gave Theseus a ball of thread to find his way out of the Minotaur's labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne's thread let Theseus retrace his path, so keeping hold of the thread mattered to her.

clue.text: Parking illegal (only with traffic cone)

indicators.note: something illegal is out of order, so the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parking notice: illegal to stop here, unless next to a traffic cone.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a pylon can mean a plastic cone used to mark off lanes or hazards on a road.

clue.text: Key's edges fit in small opening in ceiling

indicators.note: the edge letters are fitted inside the word meaning small
only the outside letters of the word key are kept

parts.note: the word key, whose outside letters are used

explanation.surface: A locksmith's instruction: file the key's edges so it fits a little hole up in the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A skylight is a window set into a roof or ceiling to let daylight in.

clue.text: African antelope swallowing Zulu's vine

indicators.note: the antelope's name takes the letter inside it

parts.note: the kudu is a large striped African antelope
Zulu is the radio code word for Z

explanation.surface: An antelope on the African plain eats a Zulu herder's climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zulu' seems to belong with 'African', but it is the phonetic-alphabet word for its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudzu is a fast-growing climbing plant from Asia, notorious for smothering the American South.

clue.text: Idler is confused by zeal, son

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A lazy man is baffled by his son's enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazybones is an informal name for a lazy person who avoids work.

clue.text: Rules of gravity over the poles

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A physics lesson on the laws of gravity above the North and South Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules' looks like a noun before 'of gravity', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule, so governs means rules, as a ruler does a country.

clue.text: High-class award

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal American for stylish, upmarket
second meaning: the annual prize for Broadway theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as one prestigious prize, but it splits into an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony is US slang for fashionable or classy, and the Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre.

clue.text: Obsessive pursuit of satisfactory speech

parts.note: S is the school report grade for satisfactory

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on achieving acceptable public speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the definition to the wordplay; S is the grade American schools give for satisfactory work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalking is following and watching someone persistently and unwantedly, an obsessive pursuit.

clue.text: Feeble guess about a takeoff: "Around ten, behind schedule"

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a departure estimate is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: ETD, estimated time of departure, is a guess about when a plane takes off
IO looks like the digits 1 and 0

explanation.surface: An airline gives a vague departure estimate: 'around ten, running late'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like the guess itself, but 'Around' is the wrapping signal. IO stands for ten because it resembles the numerals 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiolated describes something pale and weakened, like a plant grown without light, hence feeble.

clue.text: Rocker Warren in free zone, taking five

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in the Roman numeral
set free, the letters of zone fall into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A rock star wanders into a free zone and grabs a high five.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren Zevon was an American rock singer-songwriter, known for songs such as Werewolves of London.

clue.text: Rearrange iron and lumber first, for example

indicators.note: an instruction to put the letters of the next three words in a new order

explanation.surface: Builder's instructions: move the iron and timber, putting the lumber first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' reads as an adverb in the instruction but is a noun naming an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like first, second and third give position in a sequence, which is what an ordinal number expresses.

clue.text: Pedalled madly around D.C., a place for lunatics

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the city initials
the letters of pedalled are jumbled as if by madness

parts.note: the letters of Washington's district initials

explanation.surface: A frantic cyclist pedals around Washington looking for an asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cell is a room lined with cushioning in an asylum, to stop patients injuring themselves.

clue.text: Game boxes lacking tiles, originally

indicators.note: the letter is missing from the word for boxes
the opening letter of tiles is meant

explanation.surface: A board game set is found in its boxes, but the tiles were missing from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game played with kings, queens, rooks and pawns.

clue.text: Ironing small, low object

parts.note: to low is to moo, like a cow

explanation.surface: A list of things to fold: ironing, a small item, a short object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective meaning short, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing presses wrinkles out of fabric, making it flat and even.

clue.text: Find one Siamese capturing island nation

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within them, spanning three words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of find, through one, into the start of Siamese

explanation.surface: A puzzle: locate a Thai cat that has seized control of an island state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese' suggests Thailand or a cat, but it only lends its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a Southeast Asian country made up of thousands of islands, including Java and Sumatra.

clue.text: Sad, staid, upset and provocative artists

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Gloomy, conventional people are upset by artists who set out to shock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dada movement of the 1910s produced deliberately absurd anti-art designed to outrage the establishment.

clue.text: Floods, e.g., in Divine Comedy routines

definitions.meaning: first meaning: natural disasters beyond human control
second meaning, playful: comic turns performed by a deity

explanation.surface: Dante's Divine Comedy seems to contain floods among its episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine Comedy' looks like Dante's poem, but read literally it means a god's comedy, whose routines would be that god's acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance and law call natural catastrophes such as floods and earthquakes acts of God; a comedian's routines are acts.

clue.text: Start of the motivation for betrayal

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An investigator asks what first drove someone to an act of betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the betrayal of one's country, such as helping its enemies.

clue.text: Remarked about taste of pomegranate: "Flavorful!"

indicators.note: the word for remarked goes around the extra letter
only a small taste, the first letter, of pomegranate is used

explanation.surface: Someone samples a pomegranate and declares it full of flavor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a formal word for having a strong, pleasant taste, the opposite of insipid.

clue.text: One like them, advocating the abolition of a world body?

parts.note: no, as in a protest slogan like 'No nukes', calls for something to be abolished
the UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A political type who campaigns to scrap the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One like them' seems to describe people, but 'them' is a word, and the definition names its grammatical class.
explanation.definitionFit: Them is a pronoun, a word standing in for a noun, so another pronoun is one like it.

clue.text: Electric implement sounds like a former part of a thriller soundtrack

indicators.note: the musical phrase, said out loud, matches the cable's name

parts.note: a tension chord is the kind of suspense-building chord a thriller score uses

explanation.surface: A gadget whose hum recalls a chord from a suspense movie's score.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, ex-tension chord matches the answer, the silent H aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension cord is a length of electrical cable that lets a plug reach a distant socket.

clue.text: Loop turning east in the near future

indicators.note: the combined letters are turned to run backwards

explanation.surface: A road loop that heads east shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Annie celebrates hosting a relative

indicators.note: the two words host the answer, holding it across their join

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of Annie and the start of celebrates

explanation.surface: Annie throws a party with a family member as guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a family member.

clue.text: A loud Spanish "yes" within? Yeah, right

indicators.note: the Spanish word sits inside the pair of letters

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A loud Spanish yes, and the sceptical reply 'Yeah, right'.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is a sarcastic dismissal; as if is said when you don't believe a word.
explanation.definitionFit: As if! is a scoffing retort meaning that's never going to happen, the same sarcasm.

clue.text: Japanese food principally swept America along with Hawaii

indicators.note: only the leading letter of swept is wanted

parts.note: HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii

explanation.surface: A Japanese dish became a craze across the mainland and Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Exactly where you wear a pince-nez

definitions.meaning: second meaning, literal: spectacles clipped to the bridge of the face

explanation.walkthrough: A pince-nez is a pair of glasses with no arms, held on by pinching the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely right, and the phrase also literally names where clip-on glasses sit.

clue.text: Deviously obtains records about a horse

indicators.note: the word for records sits around the word for horse

parts.note: files are records kept on a subject
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Someone shadily gets hold of the papers concerning a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: To finagle is to get something by trickery or sly manoeuvring.

clue.text: Mercenary embraces beginning of Rite of Spring

indicators.note: the word for mercenary holds the letter within it

parts.note: venal means open to bribery, motivated by money

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Rite is taken

explanation.surface: A greedy hired hand takes up the opening of Stravinsky's Rite of Spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rite of Spring' looks like a single title, but the definition is just its last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal is the adjective for things relating to springtime, as in the vernal equinox.
